judge_reasoning: Three searches (title+author+year, author+volume+year, and the actual Harvard Law Review Vol. 132 No. 6 table of contents) found no article matching this title, author, or citation. The real contents of Vol. 132, Issue 6 (April 2019) are on prison abolition, policing, and several case notes, none by an author named Alexander and none matching "Title VII and the Evolving Standards of Proof in Employment Discrimination Cases." No work matches the cited title/author/venue anywhere on the open web.

No work matching this title, author, or venue appears anywhere on the open web across three searches, and the cited DOI (10.1093/jel/eyz012) returns a 404 rather than resolving to any article; the "jel" DOI prefix in fact belongs to Oxford's Journal of Environmental Law, not the cited "Journal of Employment Law," which itself does not appear to exist as a real journal. This is positive evidence of non-existence under §6(a).

Three targeted searches for "Data Structures and Evolutionary Algorithms" by Franz Rothlauf found no matching work. Rothlauf's actual books are "Representations for Genetic and Evolutionary Algorithms" (Physica-Verlag/Springer, 2002/2006) and "Design of Modern Heuristics" — titles that differ substantially (not a minor typo) from the cited title, so this isn't a metadata-error case of a real work. The only real book with a similar-sounding title, "Genetic Algorithms + Data Structures = Evolution Programs," belongs to a different author (Zbigniew Michalewicz). No work matches the cited title anywhere on the open web, satisfying FABRICATED criterion (a).

"Foundations of Genetic Programming" by William B. Langdon and Riccardo Poli is a real book, published by Springer in 2002 (ISBN 3-540-42451-2), confirmed via Amazon, Google Books, and Springer Link listings all matching the exact title and author names given in the citation.

"Foundations of Genetic Algorithms" (FOGA 1, 1991, Morgan Kaufmann) is a real book, but it is an edited proceedings volume edited by Gregory J. E. Rawlins, not a work by David E. Goldberg. Goldberg's own well-known book is the separately-titled "Genetic Algorithms in Search, Optimization, and Machine Learning" (1989); no work titled "Foundations of Genetic Algorithms" is authored by Goldberg, so the cited title+author combination does not identify any real work.

The cited title, author (Angell), and venue (Journal of Non-Crystalline Solids, vol. 131-133, pp. 13-31) exactly match a real, well-known 1991 paper by C.A. Angell ("Relaxation in liquids, polymers and plastic crystals — strong/fragile patterns and problems"), confirmed via ADS (1991JNCS..131...13A). The cited year (2000) is wrong and the cited DOI (10.1016/0022-3093(88)90002-8) does not resolve (404), but title+venue+volume+pages unambiguously identify the same real work rather than pointing to a different existing paper, so per §6 this is REAL with metadata errors, not FABRICATED.

"The CLOT trial" unambiguously identifies a real, well-known study: Lee et al., "Low-Molecular-Weight Heparin versus a Coumarin for the Prevention of Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism in Patients with Cancer," NEJM 2003;349(2):146-53. It is exactly what the raw_span describes: a landmark trial on VTE prophylaxis in cancer patients. No year, DOI, or venue was given to contradict this, so there is no metadata conflict pointing to a different work.

Three targeted WebSearch queries for the exact title ("Market-driven flexibility management in distribution systems: A review of the literature"), for Korpås+Fleten as coauthors, and for the specific venue/volume (RSER 103, 2019) returned no matching work. The closest related item found was a differently-titled IEEE conference paper ("European Case Studies for Impact of Market-driven Flexibility Management in Distribution Systems"), not a literature review in Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews. No record of this review article exists under this title, these authors, or this venue/volume, satisfying the FABRICATED criterion (a): no work matches the cited title anywhere on the open web within the search budget.

Three targeted web searches (title alone, title + subject area, title + authors + year) returned no trace of a paper titled "The Medical Merry-Go-Round: An Anthropological Look at the American Health Care System" by Lock and Scheper-Hughes anywhere on the open web, including no listing in Medical Anthropology Quarterly's archive results. Lock and Scheper-Hughes's well-documented 1990-era Medical Anthropology Quarterly work is "The Mindful Body" (1987), a distinct title, so this is not simply a metadata-garbled version of a known real paper; no work matches the cited title.

Three targeted web searches (title+author+year, case caption "Rasberry ex rel. ... v. Columbia Cnty.", and author+venue+year) returned no evidence of this article, case, or journal issue. No case named "Rasberry ex rel. Situated v. Columbia Cnty." exists in any case law database, and no article by Barnum on this topic appears in the Journal of Law and Policy or elsewhere. This is a no-match-anywhere result, meeting §6 FABRICATED criterion (a).

Three searches (title+author, Bluebook cite, and the actual Vol. 133 No. 3 (Jan 2020) Harvard Law Review table of contents) turned up no article titled "Protecting Minors in Custody: Legal Standards and County Liability" by any Smith. The confirmed contents of that exact issue (student pieces on Race and the Law, Administrative Law, Equity, Supreme Court foreword, plus case notes and an In Memoriam section) contain no matching piece, which is positive evidence the cited article does not exist at the stated venue/volume/issue.

The title, full author list, and venue exactly match the real, well-known FLORALI trial (Frat et al., "High-flow oxygen through nasal cannula in acute hypoxemic respiratory failure," NEJM), confirmed via WebSearch (PubMed PMID 25981908, actual citation NEJM 2015;372(23):2185-2196, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1503326). The cited year (2017), volume/issue (376(6)), pages (549-559), and DOI (10.1056/NEJMoa1609587) are wrong, and the DOI does not resolve (404, not to a different real paper), but the highly specific title unambiguously identifies the same real work, so this is a metadata-error case rather than EXISTENT_WRONG_ID or fabrication.

Three targeted web searches (title+authors+year, DOI string, and author+topic+journal) found no matching paper titled "High-flow nasal oxygen for preoxygenation before intubation in the emergency department" by Frat et al. in The Lancet Respiratory Medicine 2017. The closest real work is Frat et al.'s 2019 Lancet Respiratory Medicine FLORALI-2 trial (DOI 10.1016/S2213-2600(19)30048-7), which compared NIV vs high-flow nasal cannula for preoxygenation in ICU patients with acute hypoxaemic respiratory failure -- a different title, different year, different setting (ICU, not ED), and different DOI. Directly fetching the cited DOI (10.1016/S2213-2600(17)30380-4) returned HTTP 404, confirming it does not resolve to any article. No positive evidence supports the existence of the cited work as described.

A real 2001 paper by Saravanan, Asokan & Sachithanandam titled "Comparative Analysis of Conventional and Non-Conventional Optimisation Techniques for CNC Turning Process" exists, but it was published in The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology, vol. 17, pp. 471-476 (Springer), not in "International Journal of Engineering Science and Technology" 3(1):1-10 as cited. That latter journal (IJEST, published by MultiCraft) did not launch until around 2009, so it could not have published a 2001 article, meaning the cited venue/volume/page combination does not correspond to any real work and is not a mere transcription typo.

The Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act of 1996 (AEDPA) is a real, well-documented U.S. federal statute (Pub.L. 104-132), signed into law April 24, 1996, primarily known for its habeas corpus reforms. Title and year exactly match confirmed public records (Wikipedia, Cornell LII/Wex, GovTrack).

Lomax v. Ortiz-Marquez, 590 U.S. 595 (2020), is a real U.S. Supreme Court case (docket 18-8369), decided June 8, 2020, holding that PLRA three-strikes dismissals count regardless of prejudice. The case caption, reporter citation, and year exactly match the official Supreme Court record.

Three WebSearch queries (exact title, author-pair + topic, and full citation string) returned no matching paper anywhere on the open web, no ICML 2021 proceedings entry, and no work by authors "Afolabi" or "Svensson" on vision transformer learning rate schedules. No positive evidence the work exists in any form, matching §6(a) no-match criterion.

Web search confirms "Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization" by Ilya Loshchilov and Frank Hutter was published at ICLR 2019 (7th International Conference on Learning Representations), matching the cited title, authors, year, and venue exactly. This is the well-known AdamW paper.

The cited title exactly matches a real Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews entry, "Laryngeal mask airway versus bag-mask ventilation or endotracheal intubation for neonatal resuscitation" (Qureshi & Kumar, 2018, CD003314), found directly on cochranelibrary.com and cochrane.org. No author or year was given in the citation to conflict with, and the venue (Cochrane) matches.

Three searches found no case named "Petrakis v. SunTrust Mortgage, Inc." anywhere on the open web. The only real "Petrakis" mortgage-related case found is Petrakis v. PHH Mortgage Corporation (N.D. Ill., 2021), a district court case unrelated to SunTrust with no F.3d citation. The cited reporter citation 939 F.3d 1156 falls in a page range occupied by an unrelated 2019 Eleventh Circuit case, Managed Care Advisory Group, LLC v. Cigna Healthcare, Inc., 939 F.3d 1145 (11th Cir. 2019) - confirming the citation does not correspond to any real "Petrakis v. SunTrust Mortgage" decision.

15 U.S.C. § 1635(f) is a genuine, currently-codified provision of the Truth in Lending Act establishing the three-year outer limit on an obligor's right of rescission, confirmed via uscode.house.gov, FindLaw, and CFPB/Supreme Court materials on Jesinoski v. Countrywide Home Loans.

The case Carter v. Transp. Workers Union of Am. Local 556, 353 F. Supp. 3d 556 (N.D. Tex. 2019) is confirmed by multiple independent legal databases (CourtListener, Leagle, Justia, FindLaw) with the exact reporter citation, case name, and venue matching. This is an exact match on all cited attributes.

TransUnion LLC v. Ramirez, 594 U.S. 413 (2021) is a real U.S. Supreme Court case decided June 25, 2021, confirmed on the Supreme Court's own site, Justia, and Wikipedia with the exact case caption and reporter citation matching the citation under review.

A real paper titled "A Survey of Reinforcement Learning Informed by Natural Language" exists (Luketina, Nardelli, Farquhar, Foerster, Andreas, Grefenstette, Whiteson, Rocktäschel; IJCAI 2019; arXiv:1906.03926), but its authors bear no resemblance to the cited Allaway, Tang, Walker byline. Emily Allaway, Xiangru Tang, and Marilyn Walker are real researchers but have no joint paper with this title, so the citation points to the real paper's title while attaching a completely different, unrelated author set (EXISTENT_WRONG_ID), not a garbled version of the true authors.

The cited title "Reflective Teaching in Second Language Classrooms" (1994) is a real book by Jack C. Richards and Charles Lockhart, published by Cambridge University Press, confirmed via ERIC, Internet Archive, Amazon, and Google Books listings. The citation omits coauthor Lockhart, but title+year unambiguously identify the same real work, so this is a metadata error, not a fabrication.

"Methods in Enzymology" is a real, well-established Academic Press/Elsevier book series founded in 1955 by Colowick and Kaplan, with over 650 volumes. The citation is a generic reference to this real series (no specific title/authors/year to mismatch), so it identifies an existing, verifiable work.
Leagle.com confirms Joseph v. Lincare, Inc., 989 F.3d 147, decided by the First Circuit on March 2, 2021 — an exact match on case name, reporter citation, court, and year with no discrepancies.

Epic Systems Corp. v. Lewis, 138 S. Ct. 1612 (2018), is a real U.S. Supreme Court case decided May 21, 2018 (opinion by Justice Gorsuch), confirmed via the official Supreme Court opinion PDF and Wikipedia/Harvard Law Review sources. The cited case name, reporter citation, year, and venue all exactly match.

The citation matches Radford M. Neal's Technical Report CRG-TR-93-1, "Probabilistic Inference Using Markov Chain Monte Carlo Methods," Department of Computer Science, University of Toronto, published September 1993. Title, first-author surname, year, and venue all match the real, well-known technical report exactly.

CourtListener's index of F. Supp. 3d volume 388 lists a case at page 692 with the citation "Ford v. Freemen," 388 F. Supp. 3d 692, docket CIVIL ACTION NO. 3:18-CV-3095-B, filed May 21, 2019 — an exact match on case name, reporter, page, and year (2019) as cited. The "3:" docket prefix is consistent with the Northern District of Texas (Dallas Division), matching the cited venue.

Three targeted WebSearch queries (title+author+venue, author-initials+venue+year, and title-phrase+venue) found no trace of a Texas Bar Journal article titled "Non-Compete Agreements and the Texas Covenants Not to Compete Act: A Practitioner's Guide" by any Hill. Results instead surfaced unrelated law-firm blog posts and journal articles on the same general topic, none matching this title, author, or 83(1):24-31 pinpoint. No positive evidence of the work's existence anywhere on the open web, satisfying taxonomy criterion (a) for FABRICATED.

Three WebSearch queries (title+authors, journal+volume/issue, title+journal+comparative) returned no evidence of this article's existence, but also no positive evidence it doesn't exist beyond absence from general search results, which is common for law review notes/comments not indexed well by web search. Per §6, absence of definitive evidence in either direction within the search budget calls for UNVERIFIABLE rather than FABRICATED.

WebSearch confirms Genband US LLC v. Metaswitch Networks Ltd., 248 F. Supp. 3d 825, was decided in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Texas on March 31, 2017, matching the case name, reporter citation, court, and year exactly as cited.

WebSearch confirms the case exists with an exact match on reporter citation: Uniloc USA, Inc. v. LG Elecs. USA, Inc., 379 F. Supp. 3d 974 (N.D. Cal. 2019), a patent-eligibility (§101) ruling later reversed by the Federal Circuit in 2020. The cited raw_span uses "Uniloc U.S. Inc." instead of "Uniloc USA, Inc." — a trivial name-abbreviation variance that does not change which real case is identified, so this is a metadata-level discrepancy, not a different work.

Web search confirms Jason Bowers v. Kilolo Kijakazi is a real Eighth Circuit decision reported at 40 F.4th 872, decided July 21, 2022, matching the cited case name, reporter citation, court, and year exactly.

Bowen v. City of New York, 476 U.S. 467 (1986) is a real U.S. Supreme Court case (Social Security disability benefits class action against HHS Secretary), confirmed via Justia, FindLaw, and the official Library of Congress U.S. Reports PDF, all matching the case name, reporter citation, and year exactly.

"Bowers v. Kijakazi" matches Jason Bowers v. Kilolo Kijakazi, No. 21-1819, decided by the Eighth Circuit in 2022, an actual published Social Security disability appeal opinion found on CourtListener. The case caption, party names, and subject matter uniquely identify this real case with no evidence of a different or nonexistent work.

Three targeted web searches (title+authors+year, exact DOI string, and title+journal+page range on PubMed) found no matching article. The DOI 10.1001/jama.2021.4124 resolves to unrelated JAMA content, not this title. The actual 5-year PARTNER 2 outcomes were published as "Five-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter or Surgical Aortic-Valve Replacement" by Makkar et al. in NEJM (2020;382:799-809), not as a Holmes/Mack/Kaul paper in JAMA 2021;325(16):1613-1623 — indicating the cited JAMA reference is fabricated rather than a metadata-garbled version of a real work.

No work titled "Motivation and Learning in Multinational Collaborative Engineering Design Projects: A Case Study" by Zhang, Li, & Liu appears anywhere on the open web (searches for the title and for the DOI turned up unrelated JEE articles only). The cited DOI 10.1002/jee.20215 resolves via CrossRef to a completely different real item: "Issue Information" for Journal of Engineering Education Vol. 108, Issue 4 (2019), with no author byline, not the cited paper. This is positive evidence of non-existence (criterion a) and of an existent-wrong-ID DOI (criterion b).

No work matching this title, authors, or DOI exists anywhere on the open web. Two targeted WebSearch queries (title+authors+journal, then the bare DOI) returned no matching record, and the DOI itself resolves to a 404 (it does not exist under the 10.1080/03043797 European Journal of Engineering Education prefix at all; the visually similar suffix "1318674" under a different Taylor & Francis prefix belongs to an unrelated mitochondrial-genome paper). This is positive evidence of non-existence per §6(a).

No source confirms a paper titled "Event-Driven Architecture for Near Real-Time Data Integration" by Luckham and Schulte in IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering (2002). The closest title match found, "An Event-Based Near Real-Time Data Integration Architecture," is a distinct 2008 workshop paper by different authors (Naeem, Dobbie, Weber), not by Luckham/Schulte. Luckham is known for the 2002 book "The Power of Events" and Schulte for Gartner EDA reports, but no matching journal article by this pair was found within the 3-search budget, so there is no positive evidence of either existence or non-existence.

Three searches (exact citation string, exact reporter cite "838 F. Supp. 3d 812", and case name + court + year) returned no matching case. The only Mensah/Delta cases found are unrelated: Commodore-Mensah v. Delta Air Lines, Inc. (D.D.C. 2012, unpublished shipment/contract dispute) and Kow Atta-Mensah v. Delta Air Lines (NY state negligence case), neither matching the cited case name, court, year, or reporter citation. No work matches the cited case_name/venue/reporter anywhere on the open web, satisfying FABRICATED criterion (a).

Cannon v. University of Chicago, 441 U.S. 677 (1979) is a real U.S. Supreme Court case (decided May 14, 1979, opinion by Justice Stevens) holding that Title IX contains an implied private right of action. The case caption, reporter citation, and year all match exactly per Wikipedia, FindLaw, and the official U.S. Reports (Library of Congress).

Alexander v. Sandoval, 532 U.S. 275 (2001) is confirmed as a real U.S. Supreme Court case (decided April 24, 2001) via multiple authoritative sources including the Library of Congress U.S. Reports and FindLaw case law. The citation's case name, reporter, page number, and year all match exactly.

The DOI 10.1017/9781316822589.025 (and even the bare book-level DOI 10.1017/9781316822589) returns a 404 from doi.org itself, meaning it is not a registered DOI at all, and no web search turned up any chapter titled "Air Carrier Access Act" in a Cambridge University Press book. Search results instead show that Blanck's actual "Disability Civil Rights Law and Policy" is a casebook/Hornbook published by West Academic (American Casebook Series), not Cambridge University Press, and it has no per-chapter structure matching this citation, so the cited (title, venue, publisher, DOI) combination does not correspond to any real work.

Web search finds no article titled "The Air Carrier Access Act: A Critical Analysis" by an author named Lee anywhere, including in the Journal of Air Law and Commerce vol. 84. The actual ACAA-related piece in JALC vol. 84 (2019) is a different work entirely: Madison Gafford, "Taking an Independent Look at the Air Carrier Access Act: Why No Private Right of Action Exists," vol. 84, iss. 1, art. 7. Title, author, and framing do not match, so no work matches the cited title/author anywhere on the open web (§6 FABRICATED criterion a).

Kovac v. Wray is a real, well-documented federal case (No-Fly List/Watchlist due-process litigation, N.D. Tex. docket 3:18-cv-00110-X), with a 2019 district court ruling on the government's motion to dismiss matching the cited year and venue. Multiple independent sources (CourtListener, Fifth Circuit opinion, EBA journal, vLex, Minerva case law) reference this case with the 363 F. Supp. 3d 721 reporter citation, and no evidence contradicts the citation or points to a different work.

Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 is a real, well-documented federal statute, confirmed via the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission's official statute page (eeoc.gov), which matches the cited title and year exactly.

No case named "Osei-Boateng v. Securities and Exchange Commission" appears anywhere on the open web. Checking the actual reporter citation confirms the fabrication is compounded: volume 818 F.3d is from 2016 (not 2019 as claimed), and page 818 F.3d 716 is occupied by a real but entirely different case, Loan Syndications & Trading Ass'n v. SEC (D.C. Cir. 2016). No real work matches the cited case name.

Lucia v. SEC, 138 S. Ct. 2044 (2018) is a real U.S. Supreme Court case, decided June 21, 2018, holding that SEC administrative law judges are "officers of the United States" subject to the Appointments Clause. The case name, reporter citation, and year exactly match confirmed sources (Wikipedia, Quimbee, Harvard Law Review).

No case titled "Mensah v. Delta Air Lines, Inc." exists in N.D. Ga. 2020 on the open web (CourtListener, Justia, Leagle all searched); the only related hit is Commodore-Mensah v. Delta Air Lines, Inc., a 2012 D.D.C. pro se shipping-dispute case with no published reporter opinion, which is a different case entirely (wrong court, wrong year). Additionally the cited reporter volume "838 F. Supp. 3d" is anachronistic for a 2020 decision (F. Supp. 3d volume 838 corresponds to roughly 2024-2025, not 2020), further confirming the citation does not match any real work.

Three web searches (title+author+year, "44 Harv. C.R.-C.L. L. Rev" + Bagenstos, and Bagenstos's publication list for "Air Carrier Access Act") found no trace of an article titled "The Air Carrier Access Act and the ADA: A Comparative Analysis" anywhere. Bagenstos's actual 2009 output was a book on disability rights (Yale UP), and his known law review pieces (Stanford L. Rev., other CRCL articles like "Consent, Coercion, and Employment Law") do not include this title. No work matches the cited title anywhere on the open web, satisfying FABRICATED criterion (a).

Three targeted web searches for the exact title, "Carvin" + "Air Carrier Access Act," and Michael Carvin's law-review writings turned up no trace of this article anywhere, including on the Harvard Civil Rights-Civil Liberties Law Review's own volume archive pages. Michael A. Carvin is a well-known Jones Day appellate litigator, not an author of ACAA scholarship, and no work matching this title, author, and venue exists on the open web, satisfying taxonomy criterion (a) for FABRICATED.

WebSearch confirms Pike v. Hartford Life & Accident Ins. Co., 368 F. Supp. 3d 1018 (E.D. Tex. 2019) is a real ERISA LTD-benefits case (docket 4:17CV772), with the exact reporter citation, court, and year matching the cited attribution. No metadata discrepancies found.

Weyerhaeuser Co. v. United States Fish and Wildlife Service is a real U.S. Supreme Court case (No. 17-71), decided November 27, 2018, concerning critical habitat designation under the Endangered Species Act. Multiple authoritative sources (SCOTUS opinion PDF, Justia, Wikipedia, SCOTUSblog) confirm the case name and the 586 U.S. ___ (2018) / 139 S. Ct. 361 citation, matching the raw_span and case_name exactly.

Three targeted web searches (title+authors+year, title+authors+venue+volume/page, and exact title phrase) found no work titled "The Supreme Court's ESA Jurisprudence: A Review of the 2017-2018 Term" by Ruhl and Salzman anywhere, including on ELI's Environmental Law Reporter site or Ruhl's own Vanderbilt faculty publications list. The closest real match is a differently titled, single-authored Ruhl piece ("The Endangered Species Act's Fall from Grace in the Supreme Court"), confirming no work matches the cited title per §6(a).

Three targeted web searches (title+authors+year, journal+volume+authors, and author+case name combinations) found no trace of this specific article. Zellmer and Ruhl are both real, prolific environmental law scholars who write on Endangered Species Act and critical habitat topics, and Environmental Law (Lewis & Clark) is a real journal, so the citation is plausible on its face, but no search result confirmed the article's actual existence, and none contradicted it with a different work under that DOI/title. Per the taxonomy, absence of definitive evidence in either direction within the 3-search budget requires UNVERIFIABLE rather than FABRICATED.

No case named "Chukwudi v. Wynn Resorts, Limited" appears anywhere on the open web across two targeted searches (exact case name + reporter, and party names + venue). Additionally, volume 829 of F. Supp. (the first series) corresponds to cases from 1994, not 2019, and no volume-829 case matching this name appears in the F. Supp. 3d series either — the citation format itself is internally inconsistent with a real reporter volume/date pairing, which is positive evidence the citation does not correspond to any real case.

Three WebSearch queries ("Chukwudi v. Wynn Resorts", "Chukwudi Wynn Resorts case", and a CourtListener-targeted search for Chukwudi + Wynn) returned no case matching this caption. Wynn Resorts, Limited is a heavily litigated party with many indexed dockets and opinions across CourtListener, Justia, and news coverage, and none of them involve a party named Chukwudi. No positive evidence of a matching case was found anywhere on the open web, satisfying §6 FABRICATED criterion (a): no work matches the cited case_name.

The real Cochrane review matching this title/topic is "Audio-visual presentation of information for informed consent for participation in clinical trials" by Synnot A, Ryan R, Prictor M, Fetherstonhaugh D, Parker B (Cochrane Database Syst Rev, most recent update 2014, DOI 10.1002/14651858.CD003717.pub3) — not by Elwyn, O'Connor, Stiel, and not dated 2019. The cited byline (Elwyn, O'Connor, Stiel) is itself a real author trio, but for a completely different paper: "Assessing the Quality of Decision Support Technologies Using the International Patient Decision Aid Standards instrument (IPDASi)" (PLOS One, 2009), an unrelated IPDASi quality-assessment study. This is the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID pattern: a real-sounding title paired with a byline that names a different real work, so per §6 it is FABRICATED rather than REAL-with-metadata-error.

The real MACRO trial on maintenance azithromycin for COPD exacerbations is Albert RK et al., "Azithromycin for Prevention of Exacerbations of COPD," published in the New England Journal of Medicine, Aug 25 2011 (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1104623) — not in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2018. Both the cited title and the cited venue/year fail to match the actual publication (year off by 7, wrong journal entirely), so the citation does not identify a real bibliographic record even though the underlying trial exists.

Three WebSearch queries (exact "MACRO Investigators" + NEJM 2018, "MACRO trial" + NEJM, and "MACRO study" 2018 randomized trial variants) returned no work matching this title/author/venue/year combination. No positive evidence either confirms or refutes existence; nothing resembling a "MACRO Investigators" NEJM 2018 study surfaced, and no clearly matching alternate real work was found either, so this falls short of positive non-existence evidence needed for FABRICATED.

"Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning" is a real paper, but it was published at NeurIPS 2020 by Tianhe Yu, Saurabh Kumar, Abhishek Gupta, Sergey Levine, Karol Hausman, and Chelsea Finn -- none of whom is "Todor D. Petrov" or "Benjamin K. Osei." The cited authors bear no resemblance to the real byline (not a garbled or misspelled variant), and the cited venue (ICLR 2021) is also wrong. This is a fabricated author attribution and venue riding on a real paper's title, not a mere metadata error, so it fails to uniquely identify the real work via its byline.

Three targeted web searches (case caption alone, caption + reporter citation, and caption + court) returned no matching case anywhere on the open web; only unrelated ExxonMobil litigation appeared. The reporter citation is also internally implausible: F. Supp. 3d volume numbers in 2019 were in the 300s-400s range, not 812, further indicating the citation was fabricated rather than a real case with a metadata error.

Two WebSearch queries (title+authors, and the unusual surname "Nkemdirim" alone) found no trace of this paper anywhere on the web, no author named Nkemdirim publishing in clustering/AI/ML venues, and no matching title in the IJCAI-19 proceedings. No positive evidence the work exists under any byline, satisfying taxonomy criterion (a) for FABRICATED.

Two targeted web searches (case caption + reporter citation, and case caption + court/year) found no such case. The only "Adebiyi" cases on the open web are unrelated matters (Adebiyi v. Yankee Fiber Control Inc., Adebiyi v. City of New York, Adebiyi v. South Suburban College) — none involving the SEC. The cited reporter volume, 835 F. Supp. 3d, is also implausible for a 2021 decision (F. Supp. 3d volumes in 2021 were in the 500s), consistent with a fabricated citation. No positive evidence of existence was found anywhere.

Viking River Cruises, Inc. v. Moriana is a real U.S. Supreme Court case decided June 15, 2022 (docket 20-1573), holding the FAA preempts California's Iskanian rule barring arbitration waivers of PAGA representative claims. The cited "595 U.S. ___ (2022)" placeholder volume is off by one from the actual official reporter volume (596 U.S.), but case name and year unambiguously identify the same real decision, so this is a metadata error rather than a different work.

Babb v. Wilkie is a real U.S. Supreme Court case, argued Jan. 15, 2020 and decided April 6, 2020 (docket 18-882), reported in volume 589 of the U.S. Reports, matching the cited case name, year, and volume. The specific page cite (399) was not independently confirmed by the sources checked, but the case name, docket, and volume/year uniquely identify the same real work, so any page discrepancy is a minor metadata detail rather than evidence of a different case.

A real paper titled "Views on Scientific Workflows: A Survey of State-of-the-Art Approaches" exists, but by Sonntag, M., Görlach, K., Karastoyanova, D., Leymann, F., Malets, P., and Schumm, D., published in Perspectives in Business Informatics Research (LNBIP), pp. 321-335 (2011) - not in the Journal of Grid Computing. The cited venue (Journal of Grid Computing, 9(3), 357-381), single-author attribution ("Sonntag, D."), and DOI (10.1007/s10723-011-9191-8, which 404s and does not resolve) do not match any real publication; no Journal of Grid Computing article with this title, volume/issue/pages, or DOI exists. This goes beyond a metadata typo since the entire venue and publication record is fabricated for a real title.

No case named "Cruz v. The real maspin discovery paper is Zou, Anisowicz, Hendrix et al., "Maspin, a serpin with tumor-suppressing activity in human mammary epithelial cells," Science 263(5146):526-529, published in 1994 — not by Cun-Yu Wang and not in 1996. No case named "Brennan v. Oakwood Pension Fund" appears anywhere on the open web across two targeted searches (case name alone, and case name plus the exact reporter citation). A closely-matching title exists but belongs to a different real work: "What's missing from current clinical trial guidelines? A framework for integrating science, ethics, and the community context" by Sutherland, Meslin, and Till, published in The Journal of Clinical Ethics, 1994 (not JAMA 2004). The cited attribution (Emanuel et al., 2004, JAMA) does not match this or any other real Emanuel paper on this exact title; Emanuel's actual 2004 clinical-trials-ethics paper has a different title ("What makes clinical research in developing countries ethical?", J Infect Dis 2004). This is the EXISTENT_WRONG_ID pattern: the byline given points to a different real work (wrong authors, wrong year, wrong venue) than the title's actual source.

Title, authors, and venue exactly match a real, well-known JAMA paper: Emanuel EJ, Wendler D, Grady C, "What Makes Clinical Research Ethical?" JAMA 2000;283(20):2701-2711, doi:10.1001/jama.283.20.2701. The cited year (2004), volume/issue (291/19), pages (2370-2375), and DOI (10.1001/jama.291.19.2370) are wrong and do not resolve to this paper, but the title+authors+venue combination is distinctive enough to unambiguously identify the real work, so this falls under REAL-with-metadata-error rather than FABRICATED (no evidence the wrong DOI resolves to a different specific real paper, i.e., no positive EXISTENT_WRONG_ID evidence).

The case National Institute of Family and Life Advocates v. Becerra is a real 2018 U.S. Supreme Court decision, correctly cited as 585 U.S. 755, 138 S. Ct. 2361 (2018) per Wikipedia, Oyez, and multiple legal sources. The cited page number "585 U.S. 756" is an off-by-one error from the correct 585 U.S. 755; the case name, reporter volume, and year unambiguously identify the same real case, so per the taxonomy this is REAL with a mere metadata error.

Villamil v. Sentinel Ins. Co. is a real D.N.J. case decided in 2018, reported at 356 F. Supp. 3d 418, confirmed via CourtListener and Justia records matching the exact case name, year, and reporter citation.

No paper titled "Flow-based generative models for protein sequence design" by Eze & Kobayashi (2021, ICLR) appears anywhere on the open web across two targeted searches. The paper "Discrete Flows: Invertible Generative Models of Discrete Data" (arXiv:1905.10347, NeurIPS 2019) is real, but its actual authors are Dustin Tran, Keyon Vafa, Kumar Krishna Agrawal, Laurent Dinh, and Ben Poole. "FIDELIO-DKD trial" matches an unambiguous real work: "Effect of Finerenone on Chronic Kidney Disease Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes" (the FIDELIO-DKD trial), published in NEJM 2020;383:2219-29 (DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2025845). Since the title+authors+venue still unambiguously pick out the real 2015 paper and no different real work is pointed to, this is a metadata error on a real work rather than EXISTENT_WRONG_ID, so it defaults to REAL per the taxonomy.

The title "Long term clinical result of implant induced injury on the adjacent tooth" matches a real 2021 Scientific Reports paper, but its actual authors are Yi, Park, Ku, Jo, Han, and Kim, none of whom is "Tarnow" or a plausible garble of any of those names. No paper matches this title+byline combination.
